name: LM13700
full_name: Dual Operational Transconductance Amplifier (OTA) with Linearizing Diodes and Buffers
description: Dual current-controlled transconductance amplifier, each with differential inputs and a push-pull output, plus a built-in linearizing-diode network and a high-impedance buffer per channel. The amplifier's gain (transconductance, gm) is set by an external bias current (IABC) rather than a resistor, making it the classic building block for voltage-controlled amplifiers (VCAs), voltage-controlled filters, ring modulators, and current-controlled oscillators in analog synths and effects. Successor/companion to the older LM13600, with output buffers whose DC level does not depend on IABC.

pins.name: 1 BIAS
pins.description: amplifier 1 amp bias input (IABC1, sets gm)

pins.name: 2 BIAS
pins.description: amplifier 2 amp bias input (IABC2, sets gm)

DIP-16.notes: Per TI's own connection diagram, DIP-16/SOIC-16, top view. Both amplifiers share V+ (pin 11) and V- (pin 6) but otherwise operate independently.

extra.gm_law: transconductance is set by IABC (roughly linear over ~6 decades of bias current per TI's own claim); consult the datasheet's gm-vs-IABC curve rather than assuming a fixed constant

typical_application: Voltage/current-controlled amplifiers (VCAs), voltage-controlled filters, ring modulators, current-controlled oscillators, multiplexers, and sample-and-hold circuits in analog synthesizers and effects pedals. The built-in linearizing diodes reduce distortion versus a bare OTA at higher input levels.
gotchas: gain is set by a bias CURRENT (IABC) into the bias pin, not a bias voltage; needs a current-source or current-limiting resistor from a control voltage, not a direct voltage connection
the OUT pins are high-impedance current outputs, not low-impedance voltage outputs; they need the on-chip buffer (or an external one) to drive most loads directly
both amplifiers share the same supply pins but are otherwise independent; cross-talk and layout matter in tight VCA/filter designs

the linearizing diodes need the diode-bias pin properly biased per the datasheet's application circuits to actually reduce distortion; skipping that defeats the point of using the LM13700 over a bare LM13600
